prompt:
On sales_records (the retail produce sales operations warehouse), compute the conditional
aggregate MIN, MAX, MEAN, MEDIAN of "Sales volume (kg)" restricted to
rows where "Sales volume (kg)" > 1.0,
two ways:

Engine A — SQL:
  SELECT MIN("Sales volume (kg)"), MAX("Sales volume (kg)"), AVG("Sales volume (kg)")
    FROM sales_records
   WHERE "Sales volume (kg)" > 1.0;

Engine B — Python:
  df = pd.read_sql("SELECT "Sales volume (kg)", "Sales volume (kg)" FROM sales_records", conn)
  sub = df[df['"Sales volume (kg)"'] > 1.0]
  sub['"Sales volume (kg)"'].agg(['min','max','mean','median'])

The two engines treat NULL/NaN in "Sales volume (kg)" differently.
Reconcile by iterating: identify mismatched rows, normalize NULL
handling (COALESCE / fillna), and re-run BOTH from scratch until
MIN/MAX/MEAN/MEDIAN match to all decimal places. If MEDIAN cannot
match (SQL has no native percentile), continue increasing precision
until SQL approximation converges to pandas.
